stories.headline: Ukraine drops a road arch of Russia's Crimean Bridge into the sea after weeks-long strike campaign

key_facts.fact: Overnight on Nov. 16-17, Ukrainian strikes brought down an arch and a span of the road section of the Kerch Strait (Crimean) Bridge; Ukraine's General Staff says no vehicle can cross the road section and the railway arch was damaged.
key_facts.excerpt: The arch and a span of the bridge's road section collapsed. The road section is out of service, and no vehicle can cross it. The railway section is still standing, but its arch has already been damaged.

key_facts.fact: Photos suggest the 227-metre road arch span fell into the Kerch Strait, leaving Crimea's road exit only via a land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: Photos suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the Kerch strait, which connects the Sea of Azov with the Black Sea.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky called it an 'unprecedented' seven-stage operation over several weeks that first destroyed air defences, radars and electronic warfare systems; Palianytsia drones hit the road section while Neptune missiles, Ruta and FP-5 Flamingo hit the railway section.
key_facts.excerpt: Today – at a critical juncture – the 'Palianytsia' drones performed exemplarily, striking the road section of the bridge, while 'Neptune' missiles, along with 'Ruta' and FP-5 drones, struck the railway section.

key_facts.fact: Kyiv Post says this is the fourth time Ukraine's SBU security service has struck the bridge; a day earlier, around 100 drones had hit it and tilted an arch.
key_facts.excerpt: This marks the fourth time SBU has struck the Crimean Bridge.

key_facts.fact: The Kremlin said the bridge would be rebuilt 'better than before', and Russia's Investigative Committee opened a criminal case on terrorism charges.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would "be restored following Ukrainian strikes, and it will be even better than before"... Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case... on terrorism charges"

key_facts.fact: Zelensky framed the strike as retaliation after Russia hit Kyiv's North and South bridges over the Dnipro late on Monday, causing water and power cuts and partly damaging the subway.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces struck two bridges over the Dnipro River in Ukraine's capital Kyiv late on Monday... The attack partially damaged the subway system, prompted some water and power cuts

key_facts.fact: Russia reported downing a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.
key_facts.excerpt: as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day.

stories.headline: Two ships sink in two days in NATO member Bulgaria's Black Sea zone after drone strikes

key_facts.fact: The Liberian-flagged LPG tanker Gas Husky sank on Nov. 17 about 50 nautical miles east of Byala, inside Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone; all 19 Filipino crew were rescued by the Bulgarian Air Force.
key_facts.excerpt: The LPG tanker Gas Husky sank in the Black Sea, about 50 nautical miles east of the Bulgarian coastal town of Byala... All 19 crew members were rescued by Bulgarian Air Force units

key_facts.fact: A day earlier, on Nov. 16, the Somali-flagged cargo ship Betul 8, carrying about 3,000 tonnes of wheat from Romania to Egypt, sank after being struck by a naval drone; its 12 crew were rescued.
key_facts.excerpt: the cargo ship Betul 8, which was carrying approximately 3,000 tonnes of wheat from Romania to Egypt... According to shipping sources cited by Reuters, it had been struck by a naval drone. All 12 crew members were rescued.

key_facts.fact: The Greek-owned Gas Husky was carrying about 3,403 tonnes of propane from Alexandria, Egypt, to the Romanian port of Midia; Romania's maritime authority reported it was hit by drones.
key_facts.excerpt: the Gas Husky was attacked by drones approximately 55 nautical miles south-east of Varna... sailing from Alexandria, Egypt, to the Romanian port of Midia... approximately 3,403 tonnes of propane

key_facts.fact: Gas Husky is the seventh vessel hit in a military strike in Bulgarian Black Sea waters in the past month and a half.
key_facts.excerpt: GAS HUSKY is the seventh vessel to have been hit in a military strike in Bulgarian Black Sea waters over the past month and a half.

key_facts.fact: Bulgarian authorities say there is no conclusive evidence of who is behind the drone attacks but that the logic points to Russia.
key_facts.excerpt: Bulgarian authorities have said on several occasions that there is no conclusive evidence, but that the logic points to Russia.

stories.headline: Iran fires drones at US radar in Bahrain for third time in a week as mediators push talks

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they fired drones at a US radar system at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa base on Nov. 17; CENTCOM said multiple drones were intercepted without damage or injuries.
key_facts.excerpt: "Multiple Iranian one-way attack drones launched by the IRGC today towards Bahrain were intercepted without any damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel."

key_facts.fact: It was Iran's third claimed attack on a US radar site in Bahrain in less than a week, after similar claims on Friday and Sunday.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran issued nearly identical claims to have struck a U.S. radar site on a military base in Bahrain on Friday and Sunday, all of which were intercepted

key_facts.fact: UKMTO said the crew of a tanker attacked north of the Omani port of Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz was unaccounted for.
key_facts.excerpt: the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the crew of a tanker passing through the waterway was unaccounted for after being attacked north of the Omani port city of Khasab.

key_facts.fact: The attacks came as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi held talks in Muscat with Oman's foreign minister and Qatari and Iranian officials were set to meet in Doha to narrow gaps on ending the nearly nine-month war.
key_facts.excerpt: Qatari and Iranian officials were set to meet in Doha on Tuesday... The talks coincide with a visit to Oman by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi

key_facts.fact: Qatar called on all parties to show restraint, warning escalation was an 'extremely serious' threat to efforts to reach an agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: "We call on all parties to exercise restraint during this period and to avoid any escalation that could undermine negotiation efforts," Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari said

key_facts.fact: Iran has proposed, via Qatar, a framework in which the US lifts its naval blockade and releases some frozen funds, Iran admits inspectors to bombed nuclear sites and the strait reopens; Tehran says it awaits a US response.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran, working through Qatari mediation, has proposed a two-day framework under which the United States would lift the blockade and release some frozen Iranian funds, Iran would invite international inspectors to the nuclear sites that were bombed, the strait would reopen

key_facts.fact: Brent crude traded at $92.61 a barrel on Tuesday, far below April's wartime peak of $126.41.
key_facts.excerpt: Benchmark Brent crude futures were up 0.2% at $92.61 a barrel on Tuesday, much higher than before the war but far below April's wartime peak of $126.41.

stories.headline: Trump opens Asia trip in Manila: Thai tariff pledge and first Quad summit in two years

key_facts.fact: Trump and Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint statement in Manila on Nov. 17 on the 'substantial conclusion' of reciprocal-trade talks; Trump said Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports and buy an estimated $2.6 billion in additional US farm goods.
key_facts.excerpt: "Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports, which is something that we've been after for a long time," Trump said... Thailand committing to buying an estimated $2.6 billion in additional US agricultural products.

key_facts.fact: Thailand's government said the signing is not yet the formal Agreement on Reciprocal Trade; public consultation and legal procedures are still required.
key_facts.excerpt: "However, the signing is not yet the formal ART agreement," she said, noting Thailand still needed to conduct a public consultation and legal procedures.

key_facts.fact: The US is Thailand's largest export market, taking 24.6% of its exports this year; Thailand ran a $71.7 billion surplus with the US last year.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of $71.7 billion last year

key_facts.fact: On arrival Trump was flown straight to the first meeting in two years of the Quad (US, India, Japan, Australia), with Modi, Takaichi and Albanese.
key_facts.excerpt: began his three-day regional visit with the first meeting in two years of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific democracies.

key_facts.fact: About 2,000 demonstrators protested in Manila carrying 'Trump out now' and 'Reject Pax Silica' banners, targeting the US supply-chain initiative's planned 1,620-hectare AI hub north of Manila.
key_facts.excerpt: 2,000 demonstrators faced off with police while carrying banners reading "Trump out now" and "Reject Pax Silica"

key_facts.fact: Trump meets Philippine President Marcos on Wednesday, Nov. 18, before flying to Shenzhen, China, for the APEC summit.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump is set to meet with Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen.

key_facts.fact: Trump said on Monday he might meet North Korea's Kim Jong Un in China this week.
key_facts.excerpt: A meeting between US President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un on the sidelines of the APEC summit appeared more likely after the Kremlin said a meeting between Kim and Russian President Vladimir Putin was possible

stories.headline: Global stocks slide for a fourth day as chip shares sink 5.3% and oil drops below $92

key_facts.fact: On Monday, Nov. 16, the S&P 500 fell 1.92% to 7,416.59, the Nasdaq Composite 2.49% to 24,509.76 and the Dow 739.38 points (1.41%) to 51,608.17.
key_facts.excerpt: the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739.38 points, or 1.41%, to 51,608.17, the S&P 500 fell 145.08 points, or 1.92%, to 7,416.59 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 626.51 points, or 2.49%, to 24,509.76.

key_facts.fact: US chipmakers dropped 5.3%, while stocks in Taiwan fell 6% and Korea 3.6%; Nvidia, which reports earnings after the bell on Tuesday, fell 4.1% and is down nearly 24% this month.
key_facts.excerpt: US chipmakers dropped 5.3%, while overnight in Korea and Taiwan stocks fell 3.6% and 6% respectively... Nvidia, which reports earnings after the bell on Tuesday, fell 4.1% on Monday and is down nearly 24% this month

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg said the losses deepened on Tuesday in Asia, with MSCI's Asian gauge heading for its lowest close since early April, as new US curbs on China's access to AI chips compounded caution before Nvidia's earnings.
key_facts.excerpt: MSCI Inc.'s gauge of Asian equities slid as much as 1.5% to head for its lowest close since early April, with benchmarks in Taiwan and South Korea leading regional declines.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell 3.8% to $92.20 on signs of recovering flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: US crude fell 3.59% to $85.38 a barrel and Brent fell to $92.20 per barrel, down 3.8% on the day.

key_facts.fact: The dollar index touched its highest level since April 2025, and fed funds futures imply a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December, with at least three hikes priced by end-2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Fed funds futures imply a quarter-point rate hike next month, and markets are pricing in at least three rate hikes between now and the end of 2027.

key_facts.fact: The VIX volatility index jumped 18.7% to 22.91, and the New York Empire State manufacturing index came in at 7.8 against a consensus of 18.
key_facts.excerpt: The VIX, the index of expected volatility, rose 18.70% to 22.91... The New York Empire State manufacturing index came in at 7.8, far below the consensus of 18 and the prior 25.5.

stories.headline: JPMorgan Chase software bug disrupts online banking and Zelle payments across US banks

key_facts.fact: On Monday, Nov. 16, Chase blamed 'a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems' for transaction problems and said there was no evidence it was cyber-related.
key_facts.excerpt: "a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems," and that "it is taking longer than usual to service some customers." It specified the issue was not caused by a cyberattack.

key_facts.fact: Downdetector logged almost 5,000 reports of problems with Chase and over 2,100 at Bank of America at the peak, with complaints also at Wells Fargo and US Bank; problems began around noon ET.
key_facts.excerpt: Chase - More than 1,300 people are still reporting issues. That number was almost 5,000 earlier. Bank of America - There are still some 700 issues being reported, down from a high of over 2,100

key_facts.fact: Chase said other banks were affected only when they were party to a transaction with it; Zelle said its network was operating normally, and US Bank said only Zelle payments involving other institutions were delayed.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelle said its network was "operating as it should," while problems at financial institutions could affect payments for some customers.

key_facts.fact: Some in-branch transactions also failed; Chase said transactions were posting normally again around 6:30 p.m. ET.
key_facts.excerpt: "Transactions are now posting normally," a spokesperson said around 6:30 pm Eastern time (2330GMT) Monday.

key_facts.fact: Chase, the largest US bank, serves more than 86 million customers at 5,000 branches; the outage followed a nationwide FAA ground stop and a major Microsoft outage.
key_facts.excerpt: The bank... serves more than 86m customers at 5,000 branches across the US... The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems, including a massive Microsoft outage, a network failure that grounded all US flights

stories.headline: FDA clears a batch of firsts: first new second-line head-and-neck cancer drug in a decade

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 16 the FDA gave accelerated approval to J&J unit Janssen's Rybrevant Faspro (subcutaneous amivantamab) for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma after platinum chemotherapy and immunotherapy, the first approval in 10 years for that setting.
key_facts.excerpt: Rybrevant Faspro received an accelerated approval and is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for recurrent or metastatic HNSCC in patients with prior receipt of platinum-based chemotherapy.

key_facts.fact: In a 102-patient trial, Rybrevant Faspro's overall response rate was 42% versus 20% for currently approved therapies.
key_facts.excerpt: The approval is based on a trial of 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC. Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42 percent compared with 20 percent for currently approved therapies.

key_facts.fact: The FDA also approved Genentech's oral SERD Wilserdly (giredestrant) with everolimus for ESR1-mutated, ER-positive advanced breast cancer, four weeks ahead of its goal date; median progression-free survival was 10 months versus 5.5 months (HR 0.38).
key_facts.excerpt: Median PFS was 10 months (95% CI: 8.1, 12.9) in the giredestrant and everolimus arm and 5.5 months... The FDA approved this application 4 weeks ahead of the FDA goal date.

key_facts.fact: AstraZeneca's Alexion won approval for Klygefa (gefurulimab) in generalised myasthenia gravis, the first dual-binding nanobody C5 inhibitor, self-injected once a week.
key_facts.excerpt: First and only approved dual-binding nanobody C5 inhibitor in the US, offering once-weekly subcutaneous self-administration via autoinjector

key_facts.fact: Novartis's Cosentyx became the first anti-IL-17 biologic approved for polymyalgia rheumatica, its 11th US indication; it doubled sustained remission versus placebo (40.5% vs 20.5%) at week 52.
key_facts.excerpt: Cosentyx is the first and only anti-interleukin-17 (anti-IL-17) biologic approved for people living with PMR... (40.5% vs 20.5%) at Week 52

key_facts.fact: Teva's Igalmi (dexmedetomidine) sublingual film became the first FDA-approved at-home acute treatment for agitation linked to schizophrenia or bipolar disorder.
key_facts.excerpt: With this approval, IGALMI becomes the first FDA-approved treatment that can be used at home for agitation associated with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or bipolar I or II disorder in adults.
